 Kim A-lim Hits Hole-in-One in LPGA Season Finale Round 2, Retains 3-Stroke Lead
 Lee Seonghun 
 Seoul 
 Published 
 2026.11.21 10:06 
 View 
 View Count 
 Enlarge image 
 ▲ Kim A-lim 
 Kim A-lim has maintained her lead at the top of the leaderboard by showcasing peak shot-making form, which included a hole-in-one during the second round of the CME Group Tour Championship, the season finale of the LPGA Tour (total purse $11 million). 
 Playing in the second round of the tournament held at the Tiburón Golf Club (par 72) in Naples, Florida, on November 21 (KST), Kim carded one hole-in-one, seven birdies, and one bogey for an 8-under 64. 
 With a cumulative total of 15-under 129, Kim widened her gap to 3 strokes over second-place Jeeno Thitikul of Thailand, who sits at 12-under 132. 
 Having surged into first place after stringing together three consecutive birdies on the final three holes of the first round the previous day, Kim kept up her momentum by recording back-to-back birdies on the 1st hole (par 5) and the 2nd hole (par 4). 
 She picked up alternating birdies on the 6th hole (par 5) and the 8th hole (par 3) to shave 4 strokes off her score on the front nine alone. 
 On the opening hole of the back nine, the 10th hole (par 4), she missed a par putt from about 1.5 meters to record her only bogey of the day, but she quickly bounced back with birdies on the 12th hole (par 3) and the 14th hole (par 5). 
 The lucky hole-in-one came on the 16th hole (par 3). 
 Kim's tee shot landed just before the hole, rolled toward it, hit the pin, and dropped straight in. 
 Kim expressed her joy by blowing hand kisses to the fans. 
 She also added a birdie on the 17th hole (par 5) to further widen the gap between herself and the chasing pack. 
 After finishing her round, Kim spoke about the hole-in-one, saying, "When I hit the ball, I felt like I struck it a bit strongly. But the ball hit the pin and went into the hole. I was lucky." 
 She added, "I focused on the game and thought about what I needed to do. I will try to keep this flow going." 
 Yoon Ina also carded a bogey-free round with seven birdies, shooting a 7-under 65 for a cumulative 11-under 133, tying for 3rd place alongside Yuri Yoshida of Japan, Yan Liu of China, Korean-American Jenny Bae, Austin Kim, and Charley Hull of England. 
 Lee So-mi, who shaved 3 strokes off her score on this day, tied for 11th place at a cumulative 9-under 135 alongside world number one Nelly Korda of the United States. 
 Kim Sei-young, who dropped 7 strokes, tied for 16th place at 8-under 136 alongside Choi Hye-jin. 
 Yoo Hae-ran managed to shave only 1 stroke to tie for 22nd place at 7-under 137, while Amy Yang and Im Jin-hee tied for 27th place at 6-under 138. 
 Hwang Yu-min tied for 38th place at 4-under 140, and Chun In-gee tied for 49th place at 1-under 143. 
 Kim Hyo-joo, who shot an even par the previous day, struggled on this day with a 4-over 76, dropping to a tie for 56th place. 
 New Zealand-based Korean golfer Lydia Ko, who fell to the bottom of the leaderboard after shooting 5-over the previous day, continued her struggles by dropping another 6 strokes for an 11-over 155.
